buttons:
        A square button at the top of the column scrolls the list up a little,
        and a square button at the bottom scrolls it down a little. The column
        is as wide as the buttons are tall. Each button fills the column's full
        width, with nothing beside it, and is outlined by thin lines that are
        never doubled: a button draws the line down its side against the list
        and the line between it and the track, while its other sides are left
        to whatever holds the column, which draws the lines around it. The
        buttons have no background of their own: they are the colour of
        whatever the column sits on, until hovered or pressed.

    track:
        Between the buttons, a track holds a thumb as tall as the share of the
        list in view, and never too short to grab, placed as far down the track
        as the list is scrolled. The thumb is a plain rectangle that fills the
        column's full width, with no inset and no rounded corners. The track
        has no background of its own either, so it is the colour of whatever
        the column sits on. The thumb is flat, with no border or line of its
        own, as scrollbar thumbs are in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and macOS: a
        little darker than what it sits on, in both modes, as black laid over it
        rather than a colour of its own, so it looks the same on any surface.
        It darkens a step while the pointer is over it, and another step while
        it is being dragged, and goes back as soon as neither is true.
        Where there is no thumb, the track has a thin line down its side
        against the list, in the theme's border colour. With nothing
        to scroll, the thumb fills the track. Pressing the thumb and dragging
        scrolls the list with it for as long as the button is held, even once
        the pointer leaves the column, and pressing the track elsewhere moves
        the thumb there, from where it can be dragged straight away.

    steadiness:
        The thumb never jumps. Its size and place always reflect the whole
        list's real height, including a list that only draws the rows in view:
        every row is measured, even those never scrolled into view, so the
        thumb doesn't grow, shrink, or leap as rows come into view. A row that
        arrives, or changes, while out of view counts at its height as soon as
        it does, and after the list's width changes, rewrapping its rows, the
        height is known in full again by the next frame. Only what has changed
        is measured again, so a long list stays as quick to scroll and to add to
        as one that measures only what is in view; only a change of width
        measures every row again.

        A row's height is the same measured out of view as drawn in it. Text in
        a row, such as a reply's markdown, is parsed once and kept for as long
        as the app runs, not only while its row is drawn, so a row scrolled
        away and back is never parsed again, nor shorter for a moment while it
        is. Long text is parsed in the background, so a row holding it may
        first measure short: while it parses, its row is measured again every
        fraction of a second, for a few seconds at most, so the height is right
        as soon as the parse lands, whether or not the row is in view. Dragging
        the thumb, it stays under the pointer the whole way, rows coming into
        view or not.

    lockToBottom:
        A list that keeps receiving output, like a task's, adds one more square
        button below the others that locks the scroll to the bottom. While it is
        locked, the button shows as selected and the list stays scrolled to the
        bottom as output arrives. Pressing it again unlocks it. Its tooltip says
        which it will do.

        A square button at the top of the column scrolls the list up a little,
        and a square button at the bottom scrolls it down a little. The column
        is as wide as the buttons are tall. Each button fills the column's full
        width, with nothing beside it, and is outlined by thin lines that are
        never doubled: a button draws the line down its side against the list
        and the line between it and the track, while its other sides are left
        to whatever holds the column, which draws the lines around it. The
        buttons have no background of their own: they are the colour of
        whatever the column sits on, until hovered or pressed.

    track:
        Between the buttons, a track holds a thumb as tall as the share of the
        list in view, and never too short to grab, placed as far down the track
        as the list is scrolled. The thumb is a plain rectangle that fills the
        column's full width, with no inset and no rounded corners. The track
        has no background of its own either, so it is the colour of whatever
        the column sits on. The thumb is flat, with no border or line of its
        own, as scrollbar thumbs are in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and macOS: a
        little darker than what it sits on, in both modes, as black laid over it
        rather than a colour of its own, so it looks the same on any surface.
        It darkens a step while the pointer is over it, and another step while
        it is being dragged, and goes back as soon as neither is true.
        Where there is no thumb, the track has a thin line down its side
        against the list, in the theme's border colour. With nothing
        to scroll, the thumb fills the track. Pressing the thumb and dragging
        scrolls the list with it for as long as the button is held, even once
        the pointer leaves the column, and pressing the track elsewhere moves
        the thumb there, from where it can be dragged straight away.

    steadiness:
        The thumb never jumps. Its size and place always reflect the whole
        list's real height, including a list that only draws the rows in view:
        every row is measured, even those never scrolled into view, so the
        thumb doesn't grow, shrink, or leap as rows come into view. A row that
        arrives, or changes, while out of view counts at its height as soon as
        it does, and after the list's width changes, rewrapping its rows, the
        height is known in full again by the next frame. Only what has changed
        is measured again, so a long list stays as quick to scroll and to add to
        as one that measures only what is in view; only a change of width
        measures every row again.

        A row's height is the same measured out of view as drawn in it. Text in
        a row, such as a reply's markdown, is parsed once and kept for as long
        as the app runs, not only while its row is drawn, so a row scrolled
        away and back is never parsed again, nor shorter for a moment while it
        is. Long text is parsed in the background, so a row holding it may
